Thanks for flagging. Quick summary of what I see from runtime monitoring and the customer-supplied traces:

- We have repeated GPU OOMs and memory fragmentation warnings on the inference runtime fleet serving the us-west-2 region between 2026-02-16 22:00 and 2026-02-18 02:00 UTC.
- The pattern: long-context requests (8k-14k tokens) cause large KV cache growth; combined with concurrent batches this leads to fragmentation and occasional OOMs resulting in worker restarts. Those restarts produce p99 tail spikes (~1.8–2.5s) and transient 502/503 errors while requests are drained/re-routed.
- We observed pod restarts in the serving pool SVC-gpu-a and increased GC activity. No model rollout was deployed in the customer window.

Attachments: runtime-oom-trace.txt (stack traces and timestamps)

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Force fallback to the smaller quantized variant for this account for the next 24h (reduces memory footprint).
2) Apply temporary request-level limits: reduce max_tokens to 6k and lower per-account concurrency to 8.
3) Increase pool capacity or spin additional workers in Dedicated-like mode for their requests (manual routing).

I'd recommend (1) + (2) as fastest. (3) could be done if they want guaranteed throughput; requires ops intervention and may have cost implications.

I've opened internal incident INC-5241 and paged runtime oncall. Will update with root-cause timeline and a postmortem plan.

—Vivek
VP, Serving Runtime
